title: Which workspace and pane get a window from a process decade did not start?
body:
decade places a window it started itself: `scratch_open` puts the first window of its program, or of a process under it, in the scratch pane. A window from a process decade did not start has no workspace. acre's neovim plugin starts a viewer, `acre-gui --stdio`, as a child of neovim. A session tested that from an agent's shell in workspace `acre`, and each viewer window opened in a different workspace. Nothing reached across workspaces on purpose. decade had no way to tell which workspace the window belonged to.

Every window a program in a pane launches indirectly has the same problem: an editor starting a viewer, a build script opening a preview, a shell running a GUI program.

## Options

- **By environment.** decade sets `DECADE_WORKSPACE` and `DECADE_PANE` on what it starts, and children inherit them through editors, shells and double-forked daemons. On a new window, decade reads its client process's `/proc/<pid>/environ` and puts the window in that workspace. No program changes. Cost: one environment read per new window. A program that clears its environment, which is rare, loses the link.
- **By process tree.** Walk the window's parent processes up to a program decade started in some pane. Works with no new variables. A process that detaches from its parent loses the link, which the environment survives.
- **On request.** A program asks decade where to put its window over `DECADE_SOCKET`, through a command or a `decade-channel` call. This is the only option that can name a pane, such as the scratch pane or a split beside the launcher. Programs have to opt in.
- **Activation tokens.** decade hands out an `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` per workspace, and a window that presents it is placed there. This is the standard Wayland way, but many programs drop the variable before a child opens its window.

The session that filed this leans toward the environment option as the default for every window, with placement on request on top for programs that want a particular pane. The acre plugin would then work with no change and could ask for the scratch pane when `DECADE_SOCKET` is set.

## Open

- Which pane a window placed by workspace alone goes to: the scratch pane when there is one, a new split beside the launcher's pane, or a floating window inside the workspace.
- What happens to a window whose process carries no decade environment at all.
